user.title: Link your hub
user.description:
Home Assistant links to your Thalovant account, then connects to the hub you choose. The link is an outgoing connection: there is no port to open, and no Home Assistant token leaves your home.

Select **Submit** to link your account. The [guide]({guide_url}) walks through every step.

data_description.link_method: Either way, approve from a phone or computer on the same network as this Home Assistant, with any VPN turned off. **Link account** opens Thalovant in your browser and comes back through My Home Assistant. **Link with a code instead** shows a one-time code.
data_description.self_hosted: Use a dedicated connection issued by your private hub operator. Leave this off to sign in to your Thalovant account.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The link to {name} stopped working. Select **Submit** to renew it. If Thalovant asks you to sign in, use the same account as before.

data_description.link_method: Either way, approve from a phone or computer on the same network as this Home Assistant, with any VPN turned off. **Link account** opens Thalovant in your browser and comes back through My Home Assistant. **Link with a code instead** shows a one-time code.

auth.title: Approve in your browser
auth.description: Thalovant opens in a new tab. This phone or computer must be on the same network as this Home Assistant (your home Wi-Fi, with any VPN turned off): Thalovant accepts the approval only from there. Sign in if it asks, check that the request names **Home Assistant**, and approve it. This step moves on by itself once My Home Assistant brings the browser back.

no_my_home_assistant.title: Link with a code instead
no_my_home_assistant.description:
**Link account** brings your approval back through My Home Assistant, which is not turned on in this Home Assistant, and Thalovant sends it back no other way. To use **Link account**, add `my:` to `configuration.yaml` (`default_config:` includes it) and restart Home Assistant.

Select **Submit** to link with a one-time code instead.

hub.title: Choose a hub
hub.description: Signed in as {account}. Devices on the hub you choose will be able to control what you have exposed to Assist, and only devices signed in to this account can.

data_description.hub_id: Requests from this hub's devices will reach this Home Assistant. Hubs that can link come first. You can link more hubs later.

self_hosted.title: Link a private Christmas hub
self_hosted.description: Enter the secure WebSocket URL and the dedicated Home Assistant connection issued by your hub operator. Only the specified Voice connection can ask the built-in Assist agent for Christmas mirror lighting.

data_description.endpoint: Use the WSS URL at the root of your private hub, such as wss://hub.example.com. The certificate must be trusted by Home Assistant.
data_description.home_client_id: The numeric ID assigned by the hub to the dedicated Home Assistant connection.
data_description.voice_client_id: The numeric ID assigned by the hub to the Voice connection that may control Christmas lighting.

intercom_consent.title: Approve the announcement permission
intercom_consent.description:
To send announcements from {name}, Thalovant needs your approval for an extra permission (`intercom:read` and `intercom:send`, and `intercom:urgent` for urgent announcements). Nothing is turned on until you approve it, and your options stay as they are if you decline. Your Thalovant plan must include Intercom.

Select **Submit** to approve. If Thalovant asks you to sign in, use the same account as before.

data_description.link_method: Either way, approve from a phone or computer on the same network as this Home Assistant, with any VPN turned off. **Link account** opens Thalovant in your browser and comes back through My Home Assistant. **Link with a code instead** shows a one-time code.

progress.wait_for_admission: Your hub {hub} is admitting Home Assistant. This usually takes about a minute and a half.
progress.wait_for_login:
Open {url} on a phone or computer connected to the same network as this Home Assistant (your home Wi-Fi, with any VPN turned off) and approve the sign-in: Thalovant accepts the approval only from the network this Home Assistant is on. The page names the request **Home Assistant** and marks it as a Thalovant-registered app. If you are asked for a code, enter:

```
{code}
```

This step moves on by itself once you approve.

init.title: Thalovant options
init.description:
Intercom lets automations say a short text on your hub's speakers, and lets your hub play announcements on this Home Assistant's media players. Everything about it is off until you turn it on.

**Intercom is rolling out.** It may not be switched on for your Thalovant account or hub yet. If it is not, the actions say so, nothing is sent, and a repair notice explains.

**Intercom is a convenience, not a certified safety system.** It does not replace smoke or carbon monoxide alarms, medical alert devices or emergency services, and it can fail silently: a speaker offline, a hub restarting, Do Not Disturb, or a link that is down.

data.allow_receive: Play announcements on this Home Assistant
data.structured_sensitive: Allow locks, alarms, garage doors, gates, valves and sirens

data_description.agent_id: The agent that answers requests from the hub. Home Assistant's own agent only acts on entities exposed to Assist.
data_description.allow_announcements: Adds the actions `announce`, `cancel_announcement` and `list_speakers`, and an Intercom notify entity that is disabled until you enable it. Turning this on asks Thalovant for an extra permission first; if you decline, it stays off. Your Thalovant plan must include Intercom, and the hub's owner switches Intercom on for the hub in the Thalovant dashboard.
data_description.allow_urgent: Lets an announcement be urgent: it ignores Do Not Disturb and can repeat until somebody acknowledges it. Asks for its own permission. Needs announcements turned on.
data_description.allow_receive: Lets the hub play announcements on this Home Assistant, on the media players you choose next. Home Assistant tells Thalovant that this connection can play announcements, and the hub's owner must also switch receiving on for it in the Thalovant dashboard, on the Intercom tab.
data_description.structured_actions: The hub can name what it wants (power, brightness, position, temperature...) instead of a sentence, and Home Assistant carries it out on the entities you exposed to Assist. Anything it cannot resolve exactly goes to Assist as words.
data_description.structured_sensitive: Off by default. When off, these go to Assist as words, so Home Assistant's own exposure rules decide.
data_description.alarm_code: Kept here, never sent by the hub. Needed to disarm an alarm panel by voice.

receive.title: Where to play announcements
receive.description: Announcements from your hub are played with text to speech on the media players you choose, at their current volume. Choose players, areas, or both. Nothing is played on a player that is unavailable.

data_description.speaker_players: Announcements play on these media players.
data_description.speaker_areas: Announcements also play on every media player in these areas.
data_description.tts_entity: The text to speech to use. Leave it empty to use Home Assistant's default.

agent_unavailable.title: The conversation agent for {hub} is gone
agent_unavailable.description: Requests from {hub} go to the conversation agent `{agent}`, which Home Assistant cannot find any more. Until you choose another agent in the Thalovant integration's options, the hub gets an error for everything it asks.

client_key_rejected.title: {hub} no longer recognizes this Home Assistant
client_key_rejected.description:
The hub {hub} refused the security key Home Assistant uses for this link. The hub remembers the key Home Assistant had when you linked it, and this one is different. That usually means Home Assistant lost its key, for example after restoring a partial backup that left out the `.storage/thalovant` folder.

To fix it, re-link the hub: open the Thalovant integration and follow its request to re-authenticate. Re-linking makes a new connection with a new key.

hub_key_changed.title: {hub} answered with a different security key
hub_key_changed.description:
Home Assistant stopped talking to the hub {hub}: it answered with a different security key than the one it had when you linked it. That happens when a hub is replaced or reset, and also when something sits between Home Assistant and the hub.

If you know the hub was replaced or reset, re-link it: open the Thalovant integration and follow its request to re-authenticate. Re-linking trusts the key the hub presents now. If you did not expect this, check the hub in the Thalovant dashboard before you re-link.

intercom_unavailable_plan.title: Intercom is not part of the plan for {hub}
intercom_unavailable_plan.description: Announcements are turned on in Home Assistant for {hub}, but the Thalovant plan of the account that linked it does not include Intercom, so nothing can be announced or played. Upgrade the plan in the Thalovant dashboard, or turn off **Send announcements** and **Play announcements on this Home Assistant** in the integration's options.

intercom_unavailable_kid_hub.title: Intercom is not available on {hub}
intercom_unavailable_kid_hub.description: {hub} is a kid hub, and Intercom is never available on a kid hub. Turn off **Send announcements** and **Play announcements on this Home Assistant** in the integration's options.

intercom_unavailable_public_hub.title: Intercom is not available on {hub}
intercom_unavailable_public_hub.description: {hub} is a public hub, and Intercom is never available on a public hub. Turn off **Send announcements** and **Play announcements on this Home Assistant** in the integration's options.

intercom_unavailable_platform.title: Intercom is not switched on on Thalovant yet
intercom_unavailable_platform.description: Intercom is rolling out on Thalovant and is not switched on yet, so {hub} can neither announce nor play announcements. Nothing is wrong on your side and nothing needs fixing: Home Assistant checks again the next time it starts, or when you try to announce.

intercom_unavailable_hub_off.title: Intercom is off for {hub}
intercom_unavailable_hub_off.description: Announcements are turned on in Home Assistant, but Intercom is switched off for the hub {hub}. Its owner can switch it on in the Thalovant dashboard, on the hub's Intercom tab.

intercom_unavailable_unknown.title: Intercom cannot be used on {hub}
intercom_unavailable_unknown.description: Thalovant says Intercom is not available for {hub}, for a reason this version of the integration does not know. Look at the hub in the Thalovant dashboard.

intercom_can_play.title: Thalovant was not told that {hub} can play announcements
intercom_can_play.description: Playing announcements is turned on for {hub}, but Home Assistant could not tell Thalovant that this connection can play them, so the hub's owner cannot switch receiving on for it yet. Home Assistant tries again when it restarts or when you save the options. Check that Thalovant is reachable, and that your Thalovant account's API supports Intercom.

announce.name: Announce
announce.description: Say a short text aloud on your hub's speakers. A convenience, not a certified safety system: it does not replace smoke or carbon monoxide alarms, medical alert devices or emergency services. The text is spoken aloud in your home. This integration never logs or stores it; Home Assistant's own automation traces may keep it. Intercom is rolling out: if it is not switched on for your account or hub yet, the action says so and sends nothing.

config_entry_id.name: Linked hub
config_entry_id.description: Which linked hub to announce on. Needed only when more than one hub has announcements turned on.

message.name: Message
message.description: What to say: 1 to 280 characters. Line breaks become spaces. Control, text-direction and other invisible characters, private-use characters, and `<` and `>` are refused.

target.name: Who hears it
target.description: Every speaker that receives, or only the named speakers, rooms or groups.

names.name: Names
names.description: The speakers, rooms or groups to speak to when the target is not every speaker. A speaker is matched by its name, slug or id. The `list_speakers` action shows them.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: An urgent announcement ignores Do Not Disturb. It needs urgent announcements turned on in the options.

repeat_times.name: Repeat times
repeat_times.description: Urgent only: how many times to say it, from 1 to 10. It repeats until somebody acknowledges it or it is cancelled.

repeat_interval.name: Seconds between repeats
repeat_interval.description: Urgent only: from 5 to 120 seconds. Needed with the repeat times.

language.name: Language
language.description: A tag such as en-US or fr. Leave empty for the hub's default.

wait.name: Wait for the result
wait.description: For an urgent announcement that repeats: wait until it ends, for five minutes at most, before the action returns. Otherwise the action returns at once, and the `thalovant_announcement_updated` event reports each change of status.

cancel_announcement.name: Cancel an announcement
cancel_announcement.description: Stop an urgent announcement that is still repeating. The hub also stops it when Intercom is switched off or a speaker stops receiving, and a spoken acknowledgement at a speaker ends it. It works even if announcements are turned off in the options.

config_entry_id.name: Linked hub
config_entry_id.description: Which linked hub the announcement was made on. Needed only when more than one hub is linked.

announcement_id.name: Announcement id
announcement_id.description: The id the announce action returned.

list_speakers.name: List speakers
list_speakers.description: Return the hub's speakers, rooms and groups, with each one's kind, whether it can play speech (`can_play`), who is online and who receives announcements. Use it to find the names the announce action accepts. `unavailable_reason` says why Intercom cannot run on the hub, when it cannot, and `policy_synced` is false while a change may take a moment to reach the home.

config_entry_id.name: Linked hub
config_entry_id.description: Which linked hub to list. Needed only when more than one hub has announcements turned on.
